candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether downstream magnet qualification, non-Chinese feedstock traceability, and defense customer acceptance progress faster or slower than headline capacity additions imply.
candidates.next_evidence: Track DoD agreement milestones, magnet plant ramp, NdPr oxide production, customer qualification disclosures, and any waiver/nonavailability language in defense procurement rules.
candidates.node_relation: Reference anchor for U.S. rare-earth mine-to-magnet reshoring and DoD-backed compliant supply.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth mining, processing, and magnets
candidates.theme_relation: Direct beneficiary of defense and industrial policy aimed at reducing foreign dependency in rare earth magnets.
candidates.why_include: MP is the cleanest public-market benchmark for U.S. rare-earth magnet independence after announcing a DoD public-private partnership with a 10-year NdPr price floor and magnet offtake agreement.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a reference leader to benchmark smaller processors and requalification-dependent suppliers.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether White Mesa can produce separated NdPr and heavy rare earth products at commercial scale from non-Chinese or allied feedstock, and whether defense or industrial customers require requalification of that output.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify Phase 2 rare-earth circuit timing, feedstock contracts, purity specs, customer qualification status, DoD/DOE funding, and whether output is accepted into magnet or defense supply chains.
candidates.node_relation: Potential second-order processor chokepoint: rare earth separation and critical-mineral processing capability at the White Mesa Mill, not just uranium mining.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Uranium, rare earth processing, vanadium, critical minerals
candidates.theme_relation: Policy-driven demand for domestic or allied rare-earth processing could favor existing permitted infrastructure that can process monazite and separate rare earth oxides.
candidates.why_include: Energy Fuels is often screened as a uranium name, but company materials describe it as a U.S. producer of uranium and an emerging rare-earth and critical-minerals processor. Its Utah mill gives it a potentially scarce regulated processing asset.
candidates.why_underfollowed: The market label is messy: uranium/nuclear investors may miss rare-earth separation optionality, while rare-earth investors may focus on miners or magnet makers rather than permitted processing infrastructure.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AFRL-funded beryllium additive manufacturing moves from R&D into qualified production parts, and whether defense programs face limited alternative sources.
candidates.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K customer concentration, defense/aerospace revenue mix, export-control language, qualification references, AFRL milestone updates, and capacity constraints in beryllium or engineered alloys.
candidates.node_relation: Specialty-material supplier for defense, aerospace, semiconductors, and industrial applications; beryllium and aluminum-beryllium materials may require specialized handling, qualification, and customer approval.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Advanced materials, beryllium, alloys, coatings, engineered materials
candidates.theme_relation: Defense and aerospace reshoring may create demand for qualified domestic specialty materials rather than only finished systems or prime contractors.
candidates.why_include: Materion was awarded a U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory contract to expand R&D for additive manufacturing of beryllium and aluminum-beryllium alloys, directly tying it to a niche defense-materials qualification pathway.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually categorized as an advanced-materials company, not a pure defense or critical-minerals stock, so its role as a qualified specialty-material supplier can be missed in policy-theme screens.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether prototype and production orders convert into qualified defense/aerospace supply, and whether its titanium process can meet cost, quality, and volume requirements.
candidates.next_evidence: Track DoD funding drawdowns, facility ramp rates, titanium powder/component shipments, customer qualification announcements, cash runway, and any independent validation of production economics.
candidates.node_relation: Speculative domestic titanium requalification candidate: aims to convert U.S. titanium feedstocks and scrap into titanium metal products for defense, aerospace, and industrial customers.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Titanium metal, titanium powders, critical materials technology
candidates.theme_relation: If policy pressure prioritizes domestic titanium supply chains, IperionX could benefit from DoD-backed qualification and scale-up, but execution risk is high.
candidates.why_include: IperionX received a DoD award of up to $47.1 million to strengthen a U.S.-based mineral-to-metal titanium supply chain, making it directly relevant to reshoring-sensitive titanium inputs.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is not a conventional aerospace supplier yet; the opportunity depends on process scale-up, component qualification, and customer acceptance rather than established revenue scale.

evidence.claim: Defense supply chains remain difficult to see beyond tier two, while the average DoD supply chain spans five to six tiers; this supports looking for subtier specialty-material bottlenecks rather than only primes.
Tariff impacts on defense have been partly muted by national-security exemptions, but the administrative burden is greater for small companies and blind spots increase deeper in the supply chain.
evidence.source_title: A year after ‘Liberation Day,’ impact of Trump tariffs on defense industry remains muted

evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a DoD public-private partnership intended to accelerate an end-to-end U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain, including a 10-year NdPr price floor commitment and 10-year magnet offtake agreement.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense to Accelerate U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Independence

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels describes itself as a U.S. producer of uranium and an emerging rare-earth and critical-minerals company, with a strategy to build a U.S. rare-earth supply chain around its Utah facility.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels - Uranium, Rare Earths & Critical Minerals

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels released a bankable feasibility study for a planned Phase 2 rare-earth processing circuit expansion at its White Mesa Mill in Utah.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels' U.S. Rare Earth Processing Expansion Boasts Lower-Than-Expected CAPEX

evidence.claim: Materion was awarded a $5 million U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory contract to expand R&D for additive manufacturing of beryllium and aluminum-beryllium alloys.
evidence.source_title: Materion Awarded $5 Million Contract from the Air Force Research Laboratory for Groundbreaking Beryllium Additive Manufacturing Project

evidence.source_title: IperionX wins $47.1M DoD contract for titanium supply

evidence.claim: IperionX reported U.S.-based titanium production capabilities and positioned its titanium technologies for defense, aerospace, automotive, and strategic sectors.

memory_update.text: MP should remain the rare-earth reference anchor, but future passes should avoid letting it crowd out processors and qualification chokepoints.
Energy Fuels is a priority underfollowed candidate because uranium labeling may obscure rare-earth separation and permitted-processing optionality.
Materion fits the specialty-material requalification node through beryllium and aluminum-beryllium defense R&D, but revenue materiality requires verification.
Need deeper verification of which specialty-material suppliers are actually qualified on defense programs versus merely positioned for reshoring narratives.
For this node, the likely chokepoint is less the mine and more conversion, separation, alloying, traceability, and customer requalification into defense/aerospace supply chains.

summary: Expanded the universe for policy-driven specialty materials where reshoring, tariff friction, defense exemptions, and qualification requirements can shift value from obvious primes/miners toward processors, separators, alloy specialists, and domestic requalification candidates. The reference lane is represented by MP Materials as the visible rare-earth magnet anchor. The underfollowed lane emphasizes Energy Fuels, Materion, and IperionX, where exposure may be hidden by mixed industry labels such as uranium, advanced materials, or titanium technology rather than pure defense-prime classification.
